definition: Quilting point (anchoring point): the point at which the signifier stops the otherwise endless sliding of signification and produces the necessary illusion of fixed meaning. Like an upholstery button that prevents stuffing from moving freely, the point de capiton is where signifier and signified are knotted together. A minimum number of these points are essential for normality; their absence characterizes psychosis.

contrasts.differential: Point de capiton halts the sliding of signification; glissement (sliding/slippage) is the default movement of the signified beneath the signifier
Point de capiton anchors meaning synchronically through metaphor; diachronically it operates through retroactive punctuation of the signifying chain

definition: The encounter with the Real: the traumatic, missed encounter that disrupts the regular functioning of the signifying chain. Borrowed from Aristotle and reinterpreted in Seminar XI, tuché designates what lies beyond the automaton — the irruption of the Real that cannot be assimilated by the symbolic order. The tuché is always a missed encounter: it can only be apprehended retroactively, never in its moment of occurrence.

contrasts.differential: Tuché is the traumatic disruption of the Real; automaton is the regular, law-governed insistence of the signifying chain
Repetition in its deepest sense is not the automaton's return of the same but the tuché's always-missed encounter with the Real

definition: The network of signifiers in its regular, law-governed insistence: the 'engine' of repetition operating through the symbolic chain. Borrowed from Aristotle and developed in Seminar XI, automaton corresponds to Freud's repetition compulsion at the level of the signifier — the deterministic chain where the barred subject emerges and vanishes. It is the domain of law, predictability, and the pleasure principle.

contrasts.differential: Automaton is the regular symbolic chain; tuché is the Real that disrupts it from beyond
Automaton coincides with the insistence of the pleasure principle; tuché operates beyond it

definition: Negation (denegation): the neurotic mechanism by which the subject formulates the content of an unconscious wish in a negative form ('It is NOT my mother'). The content finds expression in consciousness while the subject disowns it. Verneinung presupposes a prior act of fundamental affirmation (Bejahung) — one can only negate what has first been symbolically accepted.

contrasts.differential: Verneinung is neurotic negation within the symbolic (the signifier is retained but denied); Verwerfung (foreclosure) is the primitive rejection of the signifier from the symbolic altogether, producing psychosis
Bejahung is the primordial affirmation that admits something into the symbolic; Verneinung presupposes Bejahung

definition: Transference: the attribution of knowledge to the Other, the supposition that the Other is a subject who knows (sujet supposé savoir). Wherever a subject supposed to know exists, there is transference. Lacan locates its essence in the symbolic, not the imaginary — though it manifests as love, it is fundamentally the love of knowledge. Transference is the necessary condition of analysis but must be handled uniquely to distinguish analysis from suggestion.

contrasts.differential: Both transference and suggestion operate through the same mechanism, but analysis refuses to use the power given by transference, while suggestion exploits it
The imaginary dimension of transference (love, aggression) constitutes resistance to the treatment; the symbolic dimension enables analytic work

definition: Deferred action (retroaction, après-coup): the retroactive attribution of traumatic or sexual meaning to earlier events. It is the memory, not the event, that receives traumatic significance — present events restructure past experiences a posteriori. Lacan revived this Freudian concept in 1953, using it to demonstrate that psychic temporality is non-linear: the past exists only as memories constantly reworked in light of the present.

contrasts.differential: Nachträglichkeit reveals that psychic causality is retroactive, not linearly deterministic — the later event constitutes the earlier one as traumatic
The tuché is the missed encounter in the Real; Nachträglichkeit is the symbolic mechanism by which this missed encounter is retroactively constituted as traumatic

definition: The non-communicative dimension of language that relates to jouissance through ambiguity, homophony, and equivocation. Coined by Lacan from the definite article 'la' and 'langue', lalangue is speech prior to grammatical or lexicographical organization — language in its materiality before it serves communication. Language (langage) is an 'elucubration of knowledge about lalangue.'

contrasts.differential: Langage is the structured system of language for communication; lalangue is the pre-structural material of jouissance from which langage is derived
Parole is the individual speech act within language; lalangue is the jouissance-laden material prior to any speech/language distinction

definition: Speech: the individual manifestation of language in actual speech acts. Lacan distinguishes between full speech (parole pleine) — authentic speech that reveals the subject's truth — and empty speech (parole vide) — speech that evades the truth. In the Rome Discourse, Lacan opposes parole to langage (not langue as Saussure does), making the speech/language structure distinction central to psychoanalysis.

contrasts.differential: Parole is the individual speech act; langage is the general system of language
Full speech reveals the subject's truth and transforms the subject; empty speech avoids truth through imaginary identifications

definition: Language (as general system): the abstract structure of language in general, distinguished from any particular language (langue). Lacan elevates langage to 'the single paradigm of all structures' and argues that the unconscious is structured like a language. The basic unit is not the sign (as in Saussure) but the signifier.

contrasts.differential: Langage is the general structure of language; langue is a specific language (French, Chinese, etc.)
Langage is the impersonal system; parole is its individual manifestation in speech
Langage is structured communication; lalangue is the pre-structural jouissance from which langage is an elucubration

definition: Signifying chain: the sequential, combinatorial ordering of signifiers in which each signifier represents the subject for another signifier. The chain is governed by the laws of metonymy (horizontal displacement) and metaphor (vertical substitution). Meaning is not attached to individual signifiers but is an effect of their differential relations within the chain.

contrasts.differential: The signifier is the atomic unit; the signifying chain is the sequential ordering of signifiers in which meaning is produced
The signified slides beneath the signifying chain — it is not fixed to any particular signifier but is an effect of the chain as a whole

definition: The little other (autre with lowercase 'a'): the other who is not really other but a reflection and projection of the ego. The imaginary counterpart encountered in the dual, mirror-relation. The other of the Imaginary, as opposed to the big Other of the Symbolic.

contrasts.differential: The little other is the imaginary counterpart (ego's mirror image); the big Other (Autre) is the symbolic locus of language, law, and the unconscious
The little other is an imaginary identification; objet a is the object-cause of desire that falls out of the symbolic order as remainder
